hoi4_production_shortages.description: Per production line (military and naval) the resources it was allocated per day and which of them are in deficit for the whole country. The efficiency penalty is null (not in memory). Pure read; validated:false.

hoi4_railway_build.description: Queue ONE railway with the game's railway construction mode: Shift+Click on a start node (a supply hub, naval base or the capital; the game builds the shortest path re-using existing railways) and a click on the target province. Give the start as `from_province` or `from_state` (its supply hub or naval base from the map files) and the target as `to_province` or `to_state` (its supply hub, else its largest victory point). Both ends are checked live before any input: the start must be an own railway node now (a supply hub or naval base read from the game, or the capital) and both ends own-controlled. `from_nearest_node:true` replaces a missing start, or one that is no own node, with the own railway node the network already feeds (capital, port, hub with a railway) nearest to the target over own-controlled land (the game re-uses existing railways, so the line is the same); the result says start_replaced. `to_nearest_node:true` makes the target the own railway node nearest to the given province (a railway feeds a hub, the hub feeds the provinces around it; a railway to a plain province only helps as part of the way to a hub); the result says target_node_for_province. The receipt is journaled under request_id (Verified when the own construction queue holds one more line or one more railway level; a retry of the same id settles, it never clicks again). Typed refusals before input: not_a_railway_node and end_not_controlled (both name the nearest own node), no_node_reachable (no own node reaches the target over own land: use a port, trucks or a hub), no_node_in_state, province_not_in_state, unknown_state. railway_not_queued after the clicks means the game refused the path (often: it already stands or is queued at its highest level). Railways cost 170 per level (+130 per existing level) and are the way to carry supply from the capital to far fronts.

hoi4_research.description: Fresh own completed technology IDs with bounded pagination, and active raw research counters. Progress units, days remaining and eligibility remain unverified. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_category.description: Read-only exact public folder ID association with the current own research tree, named tab, dense selection index and ordinary callback. Optional raw Sprite diagnostics; no tab switch or input authorization.

hoi4_research_extras.description: Own research bonuses that the research panel only shows as tooltips, read from game memory (no input, no lease, never pauses): limited-use technology bonuses ('free research bonus': name, uses left, bonus as a fraction, categories), limited-use cost reductions, idea research bonuses, and technology-sharing faction membership. The ahead-of-time penalty, licenses and scientist rosters are not mapped (see the not_read block; scientists belong to hoi4_special_projects). Validated live against the focus and idea scripts of the owned game.

hoi4_research_folders.description: Fresh sorted exact installed public research-folder IDs for the verified Linux layout. Native macOS returns unsupported_platform before memory reads. Independent of open GUI; canonical keys only, with no aliases, eligibility, geometry or input authorization. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_node_detail.description: One exact own current technology key: complete current-record ownership checks, target-only raw renderer/hierarchy and own detail-state diagnostics. Unrelated GUI is outside scope; no client rectangle or input authorization.

hoi4_research_nodes.description: Current own-tree nodes joined to public technology keys and conditional ordinary-control diagnostics. Full model validated before prefix filtering/pagination; default page 25. Visibility, eligibility and click routing unavailable. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_slot_control.description: One own research slot by current array index: conditional ordinary callback binding and raw typed renderer diagnostics. Optional include_geometry adds bounded Sprite cache and typed hierarchy observations. No guessed Background name, coordinates or input authorization.

hoi4_research_start.description: Start an own technology in a research slot (an empty one, or a busy one with replace:true, which switches that slot to this technology) with ordinary input (research panel, slot, folder tab, tile, Research), each click located from the live GUI and each stage verified from memory; succeeds only when the slot holds the technology. Refuses researched (code already_researched), already-assigned or busy-slot targets before any input. A tile scrolled out of view is refused. Stable request_id; every request ends in a terminal receipt (action_unconfirmed: the effect was not observed and the request is closed; read the state again before sending a fresh one).

hoi4_research_ui.description: Bounded own research slot widgets, selected slot, canonical technology Info windows, named ordinary research button state and exact render diagnostics. No eligibility, hit routing or input authorization.

hoi4_resources.description: Own strategic resources per day from memory: for oil, aluminium, rubber, tungsten, steel, chromium and coal the gross produced, available_for_production, daily need of the production lines, balance, balance (= the Production view strip number) and shortage flag, the raw ten pool slots, plus fuel stock and capacity. Imports/exports and the shortage penalty percent are null with a reason (not identified). Pure read, no lease, never pauses; validated:false (see evidence).

hoi4_save.description: Save the running game with the game's own Save dialog (Escape, Save, Save) under the name the game proposes (country and date), overwriting a save of the same name, and verify that a save file was written in the run's userdata/save games. Use it at the end of a campaign segment so the next launch continues exactly from this point (no turns are replayed). The game stays paused if it was paused.

hoi4_special_project_assign.description: Put a scientist and/or a project into one own research facility with ordinary input: Research panel (W), Experimental Facilities tab, the facility card's scientist portrait and the roster row, then the facility icon, the project entry and Start. Give scientist (name as listed by hoi4_special_projects) and/or project (key, e.g. sp_air_radar); a project needs a scientist already in the facility or passed together. Verified from memory when the facility's own scientist and project slots hold them. Starting a project spends breakthrough points of its specialization. Refused before any input: facility_unknown, unknown_scientist (closest names), scientist_wrong_specialization, scientist_busy, unknown_project, project_wrong_specialization, project_busy, facility_has_project, scientist_required, already_assigned. Refused at the screen without starting: scientist_not_offered, project_not_offered, project_not_startable. Stable request_id; every request ends in a terminal receipt (action_unconfirmed: the effect was not observed and the request is closed; read the state again before sending a fresh one).

hoi4_special_project_recruit.description: Recruit one scientist the Recruit Scientist window offers (names under recruitable.candidates of hoi4_special_projects) for political power (25/50/75/100 by how many scientists are idle). Scientists button, Recruit Scientist, the candidate's row. Verified when the character appears in the own scientist list. Refused before any input: unknown_candidate (lists who is offered), already_recruited, insufficient_political_power.

hoi4_special_project_stop.description: Stop the running project of one own facility: facility window, the stop button and the game's 'Stop project' confirmation (accepted). Stopping takes about 10 game days (the scientist stays); canceling before an iteration completes refunds the breakthrough points once stopped. Verified when the project enters its stopping state (hoi4_special_projects shows stopping_days) or the facility shows no project. Refused before any input: facility_unknown, no_project, already_stopping.

hoi4_special_project_unassign.description: Take the scientist out of an own facility (the small button on the portrait of the facility card). Refused before any input: facility_unknown, no_scientist, facility_has_project (stop the project first with hoi4_special_project_stop and wait for it to finish stopping). Verified when the facility's scientist slot is empty.

hoi4_special_projects.description: Own special-project state read from memory (no input, no lease, nothing paused): facilities (facility_id, building, specialization, assigned scientist, running project), scientists (name, skills per specialization nuclear/naval/air/land, traits, assigned_facility_id), the visible project pool (key, specialization, base_days, running_in_facility_id) and the four breakthrough accounts (points and progress percent). Specialization 'nuclear' is called Physics on screen. A new facility is built with hoi4_construction_add (building land_facility, air_facility, naval_facility or nuclear_facility). Pass rules:true to add each project's vanilla rules from the install (breakthrough cost, parent projects, required technologies, the available trigger, prototype resources, time and complexity). Use hoi4_special_projects_panel for state names and what can be started.

hoi4_special_projects_panel.description: Open the Research panel's Experimental Facilities tab with ordinary input (W, the tab), read what only the screen shows and close the panel again: each facility card's state name, research speed, scientist and project text; with facility_id also that facility's project window: every project the game offers there now with display name, type, approximate time, requirement text ('Requires a Scientist to start') and speed. Starts nothing. Needs the lease; moves the cursor.

hoi4_state_slots.description: Free building slots of own states (unlocked, max, used, free) read from each state's view (Find view centres the state, one click opens it). Use it to choose where a factory can still be queued before hoi4_construction_add. Changes nothing in the game; up to 12 states per call.

hoi4_states.description: Find states by English name (accent-insensitive substring, or the exact ID), or list every state a country owns or controls by its tag (e.g. GER), with owner and controller as the political map shows them. Pure read.

hoi4_stockpile.description: Own equipment stockpile from game memory (no input, no lease, never pauses). Per archetype (infantry_equipment, support_equipment, artillery_equipment, motorized_equipment = trucks, light_tank_chassis, ...): stockpile (pieces in storage), variants (each design in storage: type key, design_id, amount), produced_per_day (what the own production lines put out on the last daily tick, with the lines and factories behind it), fielded_need / fielded_have / fielded_short (what the own divisions need, hold and still lack: the stockpile is drawn into them first), cover_after_shortfall (stockpile minus what the divisions lack; negative = the stockpile cannot even fill them), net_per_day (the change of the stockpile per game day measured by this server over up to 30 game days; null until it has seen two game days), consumption_per_day (produced minus net), days_of_cover (stockpile / daily loss; 0 when the divisions already lack more than is stored) with depleting (false = the stock is not falling, days_of_cover null). `equipment` limits the answer to archetypes or variant type keys (a string or a list). Stockpile amounts were checked against the history files that create them; the trend needs the game to run.

hoi4_supply.description: Own divisions, the provinces and states they stand in and the supply system, read from game memory (no input, no lease, no pause). Per division: id (as hoi4_armies), army, template, state_id/province_id, hit points and percent of the template maximum, manpower against need, equipment held against need per archetype, plus supply: supply_percent (the 'Supply status' of the army tooltip, 100 = fully supplied), supply_need and supply_received per day, supply_band (full|ok|low|very_low) and the supply and demand of its province. `provinces` lists each province where own divisions stand: supply the province receives, demand placed by the units there, headroom (negative = overdrawn, the divisions there lose supply), flows from the supply nodes (node id, node province and kind when the node is own), supply hub present, railway level and naval base level. `states` gives the state's local supply and infrastructure. `supply_nodes` lists own hubs and ports with province, railway and naval base level. `below_70`/`below_50` list divisions under those supply percentages, `shortages` those with missing equipment or below `strength_below` (default 0.7) hit points, `overdrawn_provinces` the stacks that draw more than the province receives (spread them out, or build a hub or rail). Supply fields are validated:false (internally consistent, not yet compared with an on-screen reading); hub and rail throughput, trucks and trains, stored buffer and attrition are listed under `unavailable` as null.

summary.description: per-army rows, totals and the first 10 of each short list; no division rows (a few KB)

hoi4_technology_list.description: Canonical loaded public technology IDs with bounded filtering/pagination. Catalog membership does not imply player research eligibility; available:true lists only techs not yet researched whose prerequisites are all researched. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_template_create.description: Create a new own division template with ordinary input (U panel, Division Designer button, Create Empty, battalion slots, name box, Save). `regiments` is up to 5 columns of up to 5 battalion keys from common/units (infantry, mountaineers, cavalry, motorized, artillery_brigade, anti_tank_brigade, light_armor, ...; one list per column, top to bottom, no gaps); `support` is up to 5 company keys (engineer, recon, artillery, logistics_company, ...). Saving spends army experience (5 per battalion, 10 per company, 25 per extra column on this build; the cost is read from the window and returned). Refused before any input: name_taken, name_not_typable, unit_unknown, unit_wrong_slot (a company in a column or a battalion in support), column_mixed_groups (one column holds one group: infantry/mountaineers together, cavalry or artillery in their own column), template_too_wide (> 40), regiments_gap, support_duplicate, empty_template, insufficient_experience (checked before Save). unit_not_unlocked and slot_locked are found while building (nothing is saved; the draft is dropped). Returns the receipt and the resulting hoi4_template_get row (width, hit points, organisation, manpower, equipment need, ...).

hoi4_template_delete.description: Delete an own division template (its Delete button in the U panel and the game's confirmation). The game refuses a template used by divisions (also as garrison template) or by training lines; that is reported as template_in_use (with the division and line counts) before any click. Verified when the template is gone from the own list.

hoi4_template_edit.description: Edit an own division template in place through its Edit button: give the complete new `regiments` and/or `support` layout (omitted = unchanged), `priority` (reserve, regular, elite) and/or `new_name`. Only the differing slots are touched (Shift+click removes, slot click plus a choice replaces or adds). Verified from the designer's working copy and from the saved template. Templates used by divisions or training lines are refused (template_in_use) for layout changes unless allow_in_use is true: the game then reorganises those divisions at the new composition. Same refusals as hoi4_template_create plus template_unknown, nothing_to_change.

hoi4_template_get.description: Own division templates read from game memory (no input, no lease, no pause): per template the regiment columns (column x rows, e.g. [[infantry,infantry,infantry],...]), support companies, width, hit points, base organisation (mean of the battalions and companies; `organisation_live` is the same mean times the country's organisation modifier, taken from a live division of the template), manpower, supply use, equipment need per archetype (pieces), and per equipment archetype the variant a live division holds with its per-piece stats. `equipment_stats_estimate` (soft/hard attack, defence, breakthrough, armour, piercing, air attack) is an ESTIMATE summed from each battalion's main equipment variant, validated:false. Exact fields were recomputed against common/units and live divisions (hit points and manpower matched all own divisions). Optional `template` (exact name) narrows to one.

hoi4_template_options.description: Battalion and company types the Division Designer offers now (unlocked), read from its selection window (opens the designer on an empty draft and closes it again; nothing is saved and no experience is spent): per type the key, game name, group, army experience to add, width, hit points, organisation, manpower, supply use and equipment need from the definitions. Also the extra experience for a new column per group and the army experience held.

hoi4_template_rename.description: Rename an own division template (designer name box, Update). Refused with name_taken, name_not_typable or template_unknown before input. Divisions keep using the template.

hoi4_time.description: Set desired pause or internal speed 0..4 with ordinary keys (Space, keypad +/-) sent only while the owned game window is front-most, each verified by fresh memory readback. Supply exactly one target and a stable request_id; uncertain dispatches are never replayed.

hoi4_trade.description: Read the Trade view (opens it with the R key, changes nothing): the player's civilian factories and, for the seven resources (oil, aluminium, rubber, tungsten, steel, chromium, coal), balance, produced, imported, exported, special projects, production lines and needed; with `resource` it also selects that resource's filter and lists its trade partners (country, units bought now, units available as 'current/available', convoys used). Selecting a filter is an ordinary click on the view. Set a purchase with hoi4_trade_set.

hoi4_trade_set.description: Buy `amount` units of `resource` from partner `country` (exact name as hoi4_trade lists it, or its three-letter tag such as USA) through the Trade view: select the resource filter, click the partner's row, set the offer window's buy slider (a click on its track, then its arrows until the window's own 'Buy amount' reads the number) and press Send. amount: an integer (0 cancels the purchase), "max" or "needed" (the window's button that buys what the country needs). Typed refusals before anything is sent: partner_not_listed (lists the partners), amount_above_available (the window's maximum is named), trade_unavailable (the game offers no slider). Verified from the partner's contracted units in the view's Delivered column after Send (the game moves the goods with convoys over the following days; imports show in the balance table once they arrive).

hoi4_train.description: Queue `count` divisions of an own template in ONE training queue with ordinary input: the template's Train button creates the queue, its + sets each line to train one division (the game's default is infinite: a line that trains forever), then Add Unit adds the other lines in parallel; the queue gets the own state deploy_state_id as location (a queue without a location never deploys). Each step is verified on the queue in memory (amount, line count).

hoi4_wait_change.description: Block until a change after `since` arrives (optionally only given kinds or urgent ones), or until timeout_seconds (1-30) pass; then reply like hoi4_observe with woke_because change|timeout. Use it instead of polling: the reply comes within a few hundred milliseconds of the change. Pure read; never pauses.

hoi4_wait_for.description: Bounded server wait for own focus/research change, game date, research UI, or all explicit until_assignments targets. Assignment targets check the first sample too and mean active focus/current slot assignment, not completion over game time or a durable plan receipt. Choose one target family. Date/assignment waits pin the current owned worker and wake on its terminal disposition or owner retirement; lifecycle evidence is historical and proves no completion. A wait begun without a worker does not attach to a later plan. UI/assignment matches do not authorize input. Wall timeout returns only an explicitly historical earlier accepted sample; no late target is accepted. Never pauses.

hoi4_war_goal_targets.description: Which enemy-owned states to demand in the peace conference, ranked by points, industry, manpower and resources with tiers (must_take, worth_taking, optional), resource prizes, contiguous blocks, own cores and which states we already occupy. A read, not an action; the conference cost itself is not modelled. No lease.

hoi4_war_risk.description: Read-only, before justifying or declaring war on `country`: which countries would join that war on its side (its faction, every country guaranteeing it, its overlord and subjects) and which of our borders with them are not held (need a division in every border state and two per state). hoi4_diplomacy_act declare_war refuses with war_would_widen in that case unless accept_widening:true. Memory and map files only; no input.

hoi4_war_stats.description: Read-only (memory, no input, no pause): casualties per country in each war, as the war overview counts them. Each war is a group of war relations (sides inferred by who fights whom); per relation the losses of both countries (men), per war the sum per side, and per country the game's own total (the `casualties` trigger formula: sum over its wars plus the largest extra count). By default only the wars the player fights; all:true lists every war in the world. War score, leaders and goals are not read here (see hoi4_diplomacy_state).

hoi4_wars.description: Own land borders, occupied and threatened own states, from state owner/controller, own division positions and state adjacency derived from the install map files. Pure read; no lease. Stage B: wars lists the own wars (enemies, allies at war, start date) from war relations; sides, leaders, war score and justification timers are unvalidated; hostility is the war enemies plus the occupation proxy and the optional enemies tags you pass; covered is a heuristic (own divisions stand in the border states), not a front-line-order read. Alerts: own_state_occupied, border_uncovered, threatened_state_undefended. capital_land: own-controlled states the capital reaches over own-controlled land (history capital, else the largest own area); a division elsewhere is overseas (disbanding it loses 75% of its equipment).
